**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The way subresources need to be handled differs a lot between them. Right now it will replace the resource with one that has a different gvr, which means Listing doesn’t work afterwards. This PR makes it so subresources aren’t persisted which means Listing works still after a subresource create.

👋 I'd like to pick this up as it is affecting some of the tests we have. Can this please be reopened? 

I looked into the issue and saw that when a subresource is added, we replace the parent resource with it: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L107 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L404. So, both list and get are problematic after a subresource like eviction or binding is created. 

As per https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80426#discussion_r306928468, can I check if the subresource is present in the list and action.Resource is either `pods` or `nodes` and not update the parent resource?

review_comments:
I imagine removing this could introduce regression for other subresources that depend on the update behavior. How about we special case `eviction`?

nit: instead of not saving the eviction subresource and leaving the pod as it is, it seems that a successful eviction POST request should result in a pod deletion, according to https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/safely-drain-node/#the-eviction-api

> removing this could introduce regression for other subresources that depend on the update behavior.

+1. for other trival subresources like `status`, there's no "create" operation. eviction should be handled as a special case
Where should that be handled though, in the `fakeset`? Maybe here it should return an error when attempting to create a subresource, since there is no way to handle it correctly.

My original thought was something like

```
if action.GetSubresource() == "eviction" {
    return true, action.GetObject(), nil
}
```

However, I queried the discovery doc from a 1.15 cluster and below are the subresources that support create operation (there might be more, e.g. alpha features). I don't see any of them depend on the update behavior, since none of them takes a parent object (node/pod) as the body parameter.
```
,v1,nodes/proxy
,v1,pods/attach
,v1,pods/binding
,v1,pods/eviction
,v1,pods/exec
,v1,pods/portforward
,v1,pods/proxy
,v1,services/proxy
```

@bouk Could you fix the bazel build so we can see the test results from CI?

```
panic: interface conversion: runtime.Object is *v1.Pod, not *v1.Binding
```

It looks like `Binding` is broken: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/80426/pull-kubernetes-bazel-test/1154082435609137152
please run `hack/update-bazel.sh` to pass the CI
